annotations.title: Check which vehicles the catalog carries

description: Free. Check a list of up to 100 vehicles in one call before rendering any: which ones the catalog carries and under which vehicle id. Send each as the list spells it ({make, model, year}) or as a stored id ({vehicle}), with an optional ref that is echoed back. Each entry is read exactly as get_car_image would read it and answered as match (vehicle.id is the id to store and render by; vehicle.match is exact, or the looser rule that read the name), suggestion (not in the catalog as named; suggestions are real vehicles close to it, such as the same model in its nearest year, which is another car: ask the human before using one), miss (nothing close: skip it in every view and color) or invalid (error says what to fix). Use it for a catalog, a spreadsheet or any list of more than a few cars, instead of one lookup or one paid render per car; summary counts each status and the distinct vehicles a backfill would render. With views: true each match also carries views.prepared (0-9) and views.missing, which of its nine camera views are prepared now, and summary.views_complete counts the vehicles with all nine. A longer list is work for code: car-image check <file>, or client.checkVehicles, 2,000 vehicles per request.

vehicles.description: 1 to 100 vehicles, each {make, model, year} as the list spells them or {vehicle} for a stored id, with an optional ref echoed back.

make.description: Make as the list spells it, e.g. "Mazda".

model.description: Model as the list spells it, e.g. "MX-5 Miata". Send it as written: the check reads it by the image tools' rules.

ref.description: Your id for the entry (a row, a SKU), echoed back with its answer.

vehicle.description: A stored vehicle id (veh_…) to confirm. Omit make, model and year with it.

views.description: true: each match also says which of its nine camera views are prepared now, as get_image_availability reports them (views.prepared 0-9 and views.missing). Free and read-only. Default false.
